treatment.logline: Six hours before the van journey, Nimal turns evidence into personal pressure and places C-17 in Dinu's hand without securing his agreement.

arc.beat: A moral boundary meets personal leverage

treatment.approach: Tight, restrained handheld coverage with crowded garage structure behind the two men. Preserve left-right geography and normal-speed physical action. The 120-second raw bin deliberately includes master, performer and receiving coverage of the short exchange; these are editorial sources, not a demand to repeat dialogue in the assembly. Give the intended presentation breathing room through the evidence, moral objection, personal pressure and final held gaze rather than inventing events.

editor_notes: The 116-second must bin is raw coverage, not a 116-second assembly: master and singles overlap the same performances. Use each complete line only once, preserving L2, L3 and L4 in order. The 120-second scene target may require extending silent holds in post or commissioning longer clean holds; do not repeat dialogue or invent action to fill time.

Setup A maintains geography and supplies complete dialogue performances; B and C isolate the active speaker or listener; D tightens the transfer; E holds Dinu and the key together. Keep Nimal left facing right and Dinu right facing left.

Nimal and Dinu are not placed before their first scripted blocks; they begin standing on the same respective sides used later. Nimal supports the box with his left hand, opens it with his right, and transfers C-17 with his right into Dinu's left palm. The open box stays with Nimal; the key stays with Dinu thereafter.

Match the box lid opening and the 1.5-second normal-speed transfer across A and D. For the transfer, hide the meeting of hands behind the near box rim; if generation cannot maintain the occlusion, cut from the outgoing key movement to the receiving palm behind that rim. Do not attempt visible skin-to-skin contact or elaborate finger work.

L4 fills its eight-second source with a 6.8-second performance plus the clock's half-second lead and tail; there is very little extra trim room. Protect the complete line and choose the performance before placing the silent reaction.

Add the English temporal caption in post over the opening. Keep the photographs and bank documents generic. If the C-17 marking is illegible, correct it in post rather than inventing other readable text.

The silent clips are clean picture sources: build continuous roof rain, breathing and light metal sounds in post, and bridge dialogue from a chosen performer source over silent listener coverage. No music is needed for this exchange.

Speed ramp, freeze frame, digital punch-in and split screen are post-only options; the held master and singles are clean sources if editorial needs them. None is required by this intended cut. Do not slow the handoff.
Avoid mirrors, visible hand contact, fast finger work and unmotivated transitions. Hold the ending without a nod, reply, departure or other sign of agreement.

editor_notes: The 116-second must bin is raw coverage, not a 116-second assembly: master and singles overlap the same performances. Use each complete line only once, preserving L2, L3 and L4 in order. The 120-second scene target may require extending silent holds in post or commissioning longer clean holds; do not repeat dialogue or invent action to fill time.

Setup A maintains geography and supplies complete dialogue performances; B and C isolate the active speaker or listener; D tightens the transfer; E holds Dinu and the key together. Keep Nimal left facing right and Dinu right facing left.

Nimal and Dinu are not placed before their first scripted blocks; they begin standing on the same respective sides used later. Nimal supports the box with his left hand, opens it with his right, and transfers C-17 with his right into Dinu's left palm. The open box stays with Nimal; the key stays with Dinu thereafter.

Match the box lid opening and the 1.5-second normal-speed transfer across A and D. For the transfer, hide the meeting of hands behind the near box rim; if generation cannot maintain the occlusion, cut from the outgoing key movement to the receiving palm behind that rim. Do not attempt visible skin-to-skin contact or elaborate finger work.

L4 fills its eight-second source with a 6.8-second performance plus the clock's half-second lead and tail; there is very little extra trim room. Protect the complete line and choose the performance before placing the silent reaction.

Add the English temporal caption in post over the opening. Keep the photographs and bank documents generic. If the C-17 marking is illegible, correct it in post rather than inventing other readable text.

The silent clips are clean picture sources: build continuous roof rain, breathing and light metal sounds in post, and bridge dialogue from a chosen performer source over silent listener coverage. No music is needed for this exchange.

Speed ramp, freeze frame, digital punch-in and split screen are post-only options; the held master and singles are clean sources if editorial needs them. None is required by this intended cut. Do not slow the handoff.
Avoid mirrors, visible hand contact, fast finger work and unmotivated transitions. Hold the ending without a nod, reply, departure or other sign of agreement.

review.why: A structure-framed wide opening encloses the already-present men and establishes the private garage space.
A box insert gives the evidence and C-17 a dedicated, readable plane.
The locked Nimal performance, master and Dinu reaction already cover the accusation and its reception without another angle.
The locked Dinu performance and Nimal reaction already hold the moral boundary and its effect.
An isolated close reaction makes the personal pressure visible without implying Dinu's agreement.
A hand-level insert shows C-17 settled in Dinu's left palm while the box rim conceals contact.
A restrained pull-back leaves both men and the unresolved custody within the garage structure.
